transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Stocks have extended their rally following Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO.
Asian markets advancing after Wall Street surged Monday.
Nvidia's board announced Huang's return less than two weeks after he resigned,
amid an alleged Chinese spy scandal sparking national security concerns.
President Trump has taken credit for the board's decision,
but not everyone is celebrating NPR's Katie McHugh as reaction from Capitol Hill.
It's not just about Huang himself.
Lawmakers are also asking whether Nvidia shared sensitive information
or technology with Chinese interests.
Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren calls the decision to reappoint Huang reckless.
She says Nvidia's board still owes Congress answers about its compliance with export controls.
Republican Don Bacon called for Congress to investigate who approved the licenses
that will allow Nvidia to export high-end AI chips to Chinese customers.
President Trump told CNBC he personally made the deal with Nvidia's board to engineer Huang's comeback.
And Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego wants to investigate
whether members of the White House were involved in any stock trades before the Nvidia announcement.
Katie McHugh, NPR News, New York.
The Federal Appeals Court has cleared the way for the army to detonate lead-based explosives at an Iowa facility.
The army says the detonation will happen Wednesday morning,
but the status of the plan not entirely clear.
Iowa Public Radio's Grant Gerlach.
The controlled explosion of nearly five tons of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant has raised alarm
because it will create a drifting cloud of lead dust.
The judge's ruling says the EPA has taken necessary steps to minimize the spread.
Trump also says incoming Democratic Governor Rob Sand must approve the operation.
Sand says the administration should decide based on information from experts on the ground.
On social media, President Trump said he would blame Sand for any and all death or destruction
if the bomb-making material explodes spontaneously.
Sand, however, does not take office until January.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Solinsky has confirmed Ukraine's military was behind an attack
that sank a Russian warship off the coast of Libya on Sunday.
NPR's Charles Mains reports a strike, one of several, against Russian maritime targets.
The warship Mercury is one of Russia's newest naval vessels.
It was also docked at a port in Benghazi, Libya,
home to the de facto separatist government that enjoys close ties to Moscow
when it was hit and sunk by unmanned Ukrainian sea drones.
That strike followed a suspected Ukrainian drone attack Saturday
that set fire and disabled a sanctioned Russian cargo vessel traveling in the Baltic Sea.
Speaking to reporters, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called expansion
of terrorist activity in the Baltic region a dangerous trend
but declined to comment on the Benghazi incident directly.
Instead, Peskov referred questions to Russia's military,
which ignored the attack in its daily press briefing.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
This is NPR.
California Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom pushing back after President Trump
used remarks at the Justice Department Monday afternoon to slam Newsom
for commuting more than 500 death sentences in the state to life without parole.
Newsom called Trump's moral compass questionable.
Donald Trump doesn't oppose mercy. He sells it.
If you're poor, black or brown, you get the needle.
If you're rich and know Donald Trump, you get a pardon and a personal phone call.
Trump's speech marked his latest clash with Newsom,
who is considering a presidential bid.
Newsom said his decision was among the most difficult of his career.
The California Supreme Court will be required to approve most of Newsom's commutations.
A compounding pharmacy is recalling a broad range of its peptide injections.
NPR's Sydney Lopkin reports the FDA says they may not be sterile.
Greenwich RX is recalling peptides it dispensed between August 10th and September 21st.
The compounding pharmacy located in Tumbull, Texas, dispensed peptides nationwide.
The recalled peptides include BPC157, which is one the Trump administration loosened restrictions on late last month.
The recall also includes compounded weight loss medicines containing the same active ingredients as wagovi and sephound.
According to Greenwich RX, the sterility concerns arose after an FDA inspection.
The company says it hasn't found evidence of contamination, but it is initiating the recall as a precaution.
Injecting a product that is not sterile could have serious health consequences.
A list of the recalled peptides is on FDA's website, Sydney Lopkin, NPR News.

topics.text: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, drawing Congressional scrutiny over alleged China spy scandal
Federal appeals court clears Army to detonate nearly five tons of lead azide at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant
Ukraine's Zelensky confirms Ukrainian drones sank Russian warship Mercury docked at Benghazi, Libya
Gavin Newsom pushes back on Trump after Trump attacks his commutation of more than 500 death sentences
Greenwich RX recalls peptide injections over possible sterility concerns, including BPC157, following FDA inspection
